# CI fix report

## Fixed failures

- `build / common / test2`: the new shared Redisson tests referenced
  `BatchOptions.ExecutionMode` and inferred `BatchResult` in generated lambda signatures. Minimum
  supported Redisson versions do not provide those classes, so JUnit failed during discovery on
  every common test matrix job. Commit `6385b3ded0eb76286131be40cce14c0e910d2fd6`
  keeps those optional types out of method signatures and accesses execution modes reflectively.
- `build / test-latest-deps / testLatestDeps3`: Redisson 3.52.0 initializes
  `aggregatedCommands` with `Collections.emptyMap()` and passes it to its DISCARD executor before
  replacing it with a mutable map, causing `atomicBatchDiscard` to fail in Redisson code. Commit
  `6196140d22a775093b12a6e116287bdb9619e999` makes the test fixture's map mutable so the regression
  test can continue to verify instrumentation cleanup.

## Validation

- `./gradlew spotlessApply :instrumentation:redisson:redisson-3.0:javaagent:test` — passed.
- `./gradlew spotlessApply -PtestLatestDeps=true :instrumentation:redisson:redisson-3.17:javaagent:testStableSemconv --tests io.opentelemetry.javaagent.instrumentation.redisson.v3_17.RedissonClientTest.atomicBatchDiscard`
  — passed.
- `./gradlew -PtestLatestDeps=true :instrumentation:redisson:redisson-3.17:javaagent:testStableSemconv`
  — passed.
- Secret scanning found no secrets in either changed Java file.
- CodeQL skipped the test-only changes as trivial. Automated code review reported no findings,
  although its configured model was unavailable.
